title: Adaptive global expert pool with logical Mirror views
hypothesis: A two-physical-expert global pool with layer/logical-route Givens views can represent four logical top-1 routes at lower actual bytes and lower NLL than native four-expert UniPool, hard aliases, and byte-matched FiLM.

mirror_insertion.physical_object: global expert FFN weights shared across four Transformer layers
mirror_insertion.coordinate: eight Givens angles for each of four layers and four logical routes
mirror_insertion.logical_function: four route-specific functions over two physical experts
mirror_insertion.routing: per-layer NormRouter selects one of four logical routes; logical route maps to physical expert route_id mod 2; Givens acts only on selected expert input after routing; router sees unmodified hidden state
mirror_insertion.route_parameterization: view codes are learned per layer and logical route; no per-layer private expert weights

data.name: Tiny Shakespeare character corpus
data.acquisition: download only after preregistration; save SHA-256 and corpus length
data.split: raw bytes/chars [0,80%) train; [80%,90%) development; [90%,100%) audit; train/dev token windows cannot cross boundaries; vocabulary derived only from training characters, unseen characters map to one fixed UNK
data.audit_access: do not decode/tokenize/open audit span unless all development gates pass for both seeds

model.router: PA205 NormRouter with deterministic Appendix-L Monte Carlo calibration separately for logical route counts 2 and 4; independent per-layer router; global-pool conditions use aggregate pool-level balancing coefficient 0.01
model.view: 8 learned Givens angles rotate channel pairs (0,1)..(14,15) of the routed expert input
model.film_control: 8 learned group scales per layer and logical route over width 64; initialized to one

conditions: untied standard MoE: four experts owned by each of four layers
native UniPool: four physical experts, four logical routes
small UniPool: two physical experts, two logical routes
two-physical/four-logical hard aliases with no input view

training.checkpoint_rule: best development NLL among checkpoints every 100 updates

gates.quality_storage: In both development seeds, Mirror NLL <= native four-expert UniPool +0.10 nats AND complete serialized inference payload <=0.95x native four-expert UniPool.
gates.mirror_specific: In both development seeds, Mirror NLL improves by >=0.02 nats over both hard-alias and FiLM controls; payloads of controls must be within +/-5% of Mirror or report that comparison as unmatched and fail Mirror-specific gate.
gates.physical_pool: Mirror expert-bank serialized bytes must be lower than native four-expert UniPool; report whole-model bytes separately.
gates.audit: Open only if every development gate passes in both seeds. Apply the same quality and control gates on the locked audit span; no tuning.

metrics: development/audit next-character NLL and bits per character
actual serialized inference payload bytes and SHA-256
training characters, examples, optimizer updates and tokens
active expert MAC proxy and throughput
physical expert loads and router entropy

compute.measure: single-thread CPU wall time and analytic active-MAC proxy

boundaries: This is a fixed-update mechanism screen, not a capacity result.
Four logical routes are not four independent experts; count useful quality and actual bytes.
Small character-LM results do not establish production-scale expert reuse.
No optimized inference kernel is evaluated.
